decision_conditions: <p class="MsoListParagraph" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal;"><span style="line-height:normal">The proposed two storey side extension together with the existing two storey side extension on the opposite side of the building, by reason of their excessive combined width, bulk and&nbsp;massing would cumulatively form incongruous, discordant, contrived, unduly bulky and dominant additions to the host building, which would appear unduly at odds with the established pattern of development along the street scene and within the wider area, thereby detracting from the overall level of visual amenity afforded. The proposal would therefore be contrary to the high quality design aspirations of the National Planning Policy Framework (2023), Policies D3.D(1) and D3.D(11) of The London Plan (2021), Core Policy CS1.B of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012), Policy DM1 A., DM1 B. (a), (b) and (c), DM26 A (g) and DM26 E of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013) and the adopted Supplementary Planning Document: Residential Design Guide (2010).</span><br></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal;">The proposed development, by reason of the shortfall in the minimum total gross internal area of flat 4, lack of access to private amenity space for the upper floor flats, conflicts in vertical stacking and lack of information to demonstrate how noise transference between residential units would be mitigated, and lack of section drawings the to demonstrate floor to ceiling heights would result in a cramped, &nbsp;substandard and inadequate quality of living accommodation for the future occupiers. The development would therefore fail to provide fit for purpose residential units of an appropriate design, quality and layout, contrary to the high quality design aspirations of the National Planning Policy Framework (2023), Policies D3 and D6 of The London Plan (2021), Policies CS1 of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012); &nbsp;policies DM1, DM 26 and DM 27 of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013), the Technical Housing Standards Nationally Described Space Standards (2015), the Mayor of London Plan Guidance Housing Design Standards (2023),&nbsp;the adopted Residential Design Guide Supplementary Planning Document (2010) and&nbsp;Technical Housing Standards Nationally Described Space Standards (2015)<br></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal;">The proposed front garden area, by reason of the poor, cramped and in-practical layout of the cycle and bin storage storage, their prominent location and the parking space in close proximity to the entrance door and by reason of the lack of defensible space and loss of outlook and privacy to the flat 1 bedroom, would introduce visual clutter and be symptomatic of an overly intensive use of the site, to the detriment of the character and appearance of host building, the wider street scene and the living conditions of future occupiers and contrary to the high quality design aspirations of the National Planning Policy Framework (2023), Policies D3.D (7) and D3.D (10), Policies D6 of the London Plan (2021), Core Policy CS1.B of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012), Policies DM1 and DM45 of the Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013), and the Adopted Supplementary Planning Document: Residential Design Guide (2010).<br></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal;"><span style="line-height:normal">The proposal represents an over intensive use of the site by converting this single-family dwelling house into four self-contained flats, to the detriment of the residential amenities within the locality and by reason of the activity generated by the number of future occupiers contrary to policies CS1 Harrow Core Strategy (2012), DM1, DM26 and DM45 Harrow Development Management Plan (2013) and D1 London Plan (2021).</span><br></p>
description: Conversion of dwelling into four flats (3 X 2 bed and 1 X 1 bed); first floor side extension; bin and cycle stores
